references.text: Describes how the Egyptians set taskmasters over the Israelites and imposed hard forced labor on them, which directly fulfills the words that the Egyptians treated them cruelly and oppressed them with hard labor.
The Israelites groaned under slavery and cried out to God, who heard their cry of distress because of the forced labor.
God says that he has seen the suffering of his people in Egypt and heard their cry of distress over the taskmasters, and knows their pain.
Pharaoh increases the workload and makes the slavery even harsher by refusing them straw for the brickmaking work.
God promises to deliver the Israelites from forced labor and from slavery under the Egyptians.
Moses recounts that the fathers lived in Egypt and that the Egyptians treated them and their fathers cruelly for a long time.
The psalm describes how the Egyptians turned their hearts to hate God's people and acted deceitfully toward his servants.
In his speech, Stephen describes how the king of Egypt acted deceitfully against the people and treated the fathers cruelly.
God says that he has seen the oppression of his people in Egypt and heard their groaning.
